headline: Mixture models resolve cell-to-cell heterogeneity in imaging and single-cell omics
label: Mixture Models For Cell Heterogeneity
summary: Recent preprints and publications pair explicit probabilistic models with imaging and single-cell data to test heterogeneity and spatial organization.
synthesis: The common thread is explicit probabilistic structure used to recover heterogeneity and spatial organization from single-cell and imaging data. ELLA-mix applies a finite mixture model with a count-conditioned Poisson framework to separate cell subpopulations by radial RNA localization. A hybrid approach fits Gaussian mixtures of factor analyzers with cluster-specific factor numbers across breast cancer, lymphoma and brain datasets. PHM-ensemble pools ensemble mixture density estimates for probabilistic multiresolution partitioning of 1.82M immune cells. On the spatial side, spatialFDA tests differential co-localization across multi-sample, multi-condition designs, and ATAT quantifies transcription factor clustering in 4D fluorescence microscopy. ACE-OF-Clust addresses alignment and comparison of mixed-membership single-cell and spatial solutions. What is new is the move from descriptive partitions toward model-based inference, including formal differential testing layered on spatial statistics.
